result: A Hessian power method built from gradient differences, renormalized to stay local, finds the negative-curvature direction at a saddle in Õ(log n/√ε) steps; plugged into (accelerated) GD it reaches an ε-second-order point in Õ(log n/ε^{1.75}) iterations, polynomially fewer log n factors than perturbed GD.
result_plain: Gradient-only negative-curvature finding: Õ(log n/ε^1.75) saddle escape, fewer log n factors than PGD.
